problemSigns.detail: A broken spring often makes a sharp, loud noise. This sounds like a gunshot inside your garage.

problemSigns.sign: Door Won't Lift or Feels Heavy
problemSigns.detail: Springs counterbalance the door's weight. Without them, the door is extremely heavy or impossible to open manually.
Look above the garage door. A broken torsion spring will have a noticeable gap, usually 1-2 inches wide.

problemSigns.sign: Door Lifts a Few Inches Then Stops
problemSigns.detail: This indicates partial spring failure. The door cannot sustain its lift beyond the initial push.
If the cables on either side of the door appear loose or have come off the drums, it often points to a broken spring.

process.description: Our technician checks your garage door system. You get a flat-rate price quote before any work begins.
We replace the broken spring with high-cycle, oil-tempered torsion springs or extension springs with safety cables. Our trucks carry common parts.
We install new winding cones, center and end bearing plates as needed. We adjust the new springs to balance your door correctly.
We perform a balance test and safety-reverse test. This ensures your door operates safely and smoothly.
